basics.name: Lirith Vikraman N
basics.label: Full-Stack Developer
basics.summary: IT graduate with experience building full stack applications using Java, Python, React.js, Solidity, and SQL. Projects include a blockchain-based drug tracking system and an ML-powered skin disease detector. Completed a remote internship with hands-on API integration and Git-based team collaboration. Looking to grow as a full stack developer and contribute to meaningful products.

work.name: Undisclosed Company
highlights: Integrated external REST API sources into the application data pipeline, structuring datasets for downstream reporting dashboards.
Diagnosed performance bottlenecks through log analysis and documented findings for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Managed feature branches, pull requests, and deliverables via Git/GitHub in a cross-functional sprint team.

projects.name: Blockchain-Based Drug Provenance and Counterfeit Detection System
projects.description: Developed a blockchain-based drug tracking system using Solidity and Ethereum to ensure tamper-proof supply chain transparency, reducing counterfeit risks. Integrated QR code scanning for instant drug authenticity verification with a React-based frontend, addressing life-threatening risks posed by counterfeit pharmaceuticals globally.
highlights: Developed smart contracts to record and verify each step of the supply chain on-chain.
Integrated QR code scanning for instant authenticity checks through a React frontend.

projects.name: Automated Skin Disease Detection System
projects.description: Built an end-to-end diagnostic tool that ingests dermatological images, preprocesses them, and classifies skin diseases using ML techniques. Achieved high classification accuracy, providing a low-cost screening alternative to support early detection in resource-limited settings.
highlights: Achieved high classification accuracy across target disease classes.
Designed modular pipeline (image input -> preprocessing -> model inference -> result display) for easy extension with new disease classes.
